pr_title: net: tcp: Fixes for issues found with loopback operation
pr_body:
This PR brings a set of improvements/fixes for TCP operation over loopback interface (and not only loopback for some commits):

* When cloning packet at loopback driver, use a proper packet pool
* Match loopback MTU with IPv4 MTU to prevent fragmentation
* React on zero-window sent by peer
* Improve TCP stack performance when loopback is used
* Fix a bug, where TCP stack accepted unlimited data from the application in retransmit mode

Fixes #44012
Fixes #44018
pr_comments: @jukkar Thanks, I've updated the commit descriptions.

The socket in the testcase is blocking. Nevertheless the send command returns without having the complete amount of data transferred. This is resolved by calling send calls until all the data has been transferred. Is this in line with the POSIX definition of send calls?

From: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/send.2.html
`When the message does not fit into the send buffer of the socket,
 send() normally blocks, unless the socket has been placed in
 nonblocking I/O mode.  In nonblocking mode it would fail with the error EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK in this case.  The [select(2)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/select.2.html) call may be used to determine when it is possible to send more data.`

> The socket in the testcase is blocking. Nevertheless the send command returns without having the complete amount of data transferred. This is resolved by calling send calls until all the data has been transferred. Is this in line with the POSIX definition of send calls?
> 
> From: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/send.2.html `When the message does not fit into the send buffer of the socket, send() normally blocks, unless the socket has been placed in nonblocking I/O mode. In nonblocking mode it would fail with the error EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK in this case. The [select(2)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/select.2.html) call may be used to determine when it is possible to send more data.`

Yes, for STREAM socket it's ok to send fewer bytes than requested. It's not explicitly stated in the man page you quote, but it says that `send()` is equivalent of `write()`, which makes makes it clear:
>  Note that a successful write() may transfer fewer than count bytes.

@rlubos Thanks for your explanation on the expected behavior of send.

I applied your changes on top of NRF Connect SDK 1.9.1 and validated that your changes work on my embedded system. Even with 12.5% packet loss, the big transfers are correctly transferred without running out of buffers.

issue_context.title: net: tcp: Running out of buffers by packet loss
issue_context.body:
When transferring a big TCP send, packet loss causes the send to return with a NOMEM error.

The tests/net/socket/tcp has been modified to reproduce this.
The packet loss is simulated by throwing away one every 8 packets in the loopback driver.
https://github.com/ssharks/zephyr/tree/tcp_big_data_transfer
comments: @ssharks please add more information about the board you are using to reproduce this.

Totally forget to mention, I use the platform qemu_x86
Run the test using:
./scripts/twister -s tests/net/socket/tcp/net.socket.tcp.preempt -T tests/net/socket/tcp -p qemu_x86
